questions.exp: Facial fat is compartmentalized into discrete superficial and deep fat pads. Includes malar (medial/middle/lateral), nasolabial, and deep medial cheek compartments

questions.q: When performing a punch biopsy, the skin should be stretched in which direction relative to the relaxed skin tension lines (RSTLs) before making the cut?
opts: At a 45-degree angle to the RSTLs
Stretching is not required for punch biopsies
questions.exp: The skin must be stretched perpendicular to the RSTLs before punching. When tension is released, the circular defect relaxes into an elliptical shape aligned parallel to the RSTLs, resulting in a superior linear scar upon closure.

questions.q: A dermatologist identifies eosinophilic intranuclear pseudoinclusions in plasma cells on histopathology. These structures are PAS-positive and diastase-resistant. What are these inclusions called?
questions.exp: Dutcher bodies are eosinophilic intranuclear pseudoinclusions seen in plasma cells, formed by cytoplasmic invagination into the nucleus. They are PAS-positive and diastase-resistant, unlike true nuclear inclusions.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Heavy haemostat with traumatic 1x2 teeth at the tip + transverse ridges; grips tough fascia/tissue

questions.q: Identify the anatomical line or landmark shown:
questions.exp: Down-turned furrows from the labial commissures to the lateral chin. Caused by mandibular bone resorption, fat-pad atrophy, and pull of the depressor anguli oris (DAO)

questions.q: A 65-year-old male with a 12mm nodular basal cell carcinoma on the nose is planned for photodynamic therapy due to patient preference against surgery. What procedural step is strictly required to improve treatment efficacy in this scenario?
opts: Application of a 10mm margin of photosensitizer
Use of blue light instead of red light
questions.exp: For nodular BCC, prior curettage (debulking) is strictly required because the photosensitizer and light cannot penetrate deeply enough into thick tumors. This improves depth penetration and treatment efficacy, though PDT remains inferior to surgical excision for nBCC.

questions.exp: Small, fully-serrated fine haemostat (curved or straight) for clamping tiny bleeders

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a pigmented lesion on his back suspicious for melanoma. The dermatologist plans a biopsy. Which biopsy technique is MOST appropriate for accurate staging of this lesion?
opts: Shave biopsy for quick histological assessment
4 mm punch biopsy from the darkest area
Incisional biopsy through the thickest portion
questions.exp: Excisional biopsy is the gold standard for suspected melanoma as it allows complete assessment of Breslow depth, which is critical for staging and prognosis. Shave biopsy is contraindicated as it may transect the lesion and compromise accurate depth measurement, while punch biopsy risks sampling error.

questions.q: During a nail unit surgery, the surgeon notes that the proximal matrix produces approximately what percentage of the nail plate thickness?
questions.exp: The proximal matrix, located under the proximal nail fold, produces the dorsal nail plate which accounts for approximately 80% of its thickness. The distal matrix (lunula) produces the ventral nail plate comprising the remaining 20%.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Iris Forceps

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman seeks permanent treatment for axillary hyperhidrosis without injections. She is shown a device that uses 5.8 GHz energy to target the dermal-hypodermal interface. Which technology is being described?
questions.exp: MiraDry uses microwave energy at 5.8 GHz to achieve targeted thermolysis at the dermal-hypodermal interface where eccrine and apocrine sweat glands reside. It received FDA approval for axillary hyperhidrosis in 2011 and for hair removal in 2015.

questions.q: During closure of an elliptical excision on the face, the surgeon notices excess tissue bunching at one end of the wound. Which modification in the initial excision design would have prevented this complication?
opts: Increasing the apex angle to 45 degrees
Maintaining apex angles less than 30 degrees with length-to-width ratio of at least 3:1
Orienting the ellipse perpendicular to relaxed skin tension lines
questions.exp: Dog-ear deformity occurs when the ellipse has an inadequate length-to-width ratio (less than 3:1) or apex angles greater than 30 degrees. Maintaining apex angles less than 30 degrees and a minimum 3:1 length-to-width ratio prevents tissue redundancy at wound apices.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Cannulas of varying diameter for aspiration and fat transfer

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman undergoes excision of a lipoma on her upper back. Post-operatively, she develops a raised, firm scar that extends beyond the original wound margins onto surrounding normal skin. Which characteristic differentiates this condition from hypertrophic scarring?
questions.exp: Keloids extend beyond the original wound margins into surrounding normal tissue, whereas hypertrophic scars remain confined within the boundaries of the original wound. Both may respond to intralesional steroids, but extension beyond wound margins is pathognomonic for keloids.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents for excision of a painful abscess on her forearm. Despite administering an adequate volume of lidocaine, the patient reports persistent pain during incision. Which of the following best explains the reduced efficacy of the local anesthetic in this clinical scenario?
opts: Increased proportion of un-ionized drug molecules
Rapid hydrolysis by pseudocholinesterase in inflamed tissue
Decreased proportion of lipid-soluble drug form due to acidic pH
Enhanced binding to voltage-gated potassium channels
questions.exp: Infected or inflamed tissue has an acidic pH (4-6), which shifts the equilibrium toward the ionized/protonated form of the local anesthetic. This reduces the un-ionized lipid-soluble fraction required to penetrate the nerve membrane, resulting in delayed onset and reduced efficacy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a 1.2 cm pigmented lesion on his back with irregular borders and color variegation. A dermatologist suspects melanoma. Which biopsy technique is contraindicated as the primary diagnostic procedure for this lesion?
opts: Punch biopsy of the thickest area
Incisional biopsy through the most atypical portion
questions.exp: Shave biopsy is contraindicated for suspected melanoma because removing only the superficial portion compromises the ability to assess full tumor architecture and accurately measure Breslow depth, which is critical for staging and management.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: Stainless steel holder which can fit in standard razor blades. The blade is fixed by thumbscrew

questions.q: A 72-year-old woman with fragile skin and a venous leg ulcer requires a dressing that can be removed without causing trauma to the newly formed epithelium. Which dressing technology would be most appropriate?
questions.exp: Silicone-bordered foams (e.g., Mepilex Border) utilize soft silicone adhesive that adheres gently to intact periwound skin but not to the moist wound bed, allowing atraumatic removal without stripping fragile epithelium. This is particularly important for elderly patients and those with delicate skin.

questions.q: Identify the item shown:
questions.exp: Spotter retained as labelled in the source (spelling uncertain). Identify by the depicted image

questions.q: A patient presents with a heavily exuding wound following surgical debridement that is also actively oozing blood. Which dressing mechanism makes alginate dressings particularly suitable for this clinical scenario?
opts: Release of silver ions providing antimicrobial action
Ion exchange releasing calcium ions that augment the clotting cascade
Formation of hydrophobic barrier preventing bacterial contamination
questions.exp: Alginate dressings undergo an ion-exchange reaction when calcium alginate fibers contact sodium-rich wound exudate, releasing free calcium ions into the wound. These calcium ions actively augment the clotting cascade, providing excellent hemostatic properties while the dressing absorbs up to 20 times its weight in fluid.

questions.q: A riddle presented at a dermatology conference states: 'I measure 30-200 nm. I help in delivering drugs and healing wounds. I am the latest star in skin care.' What is the answer?
questions.exp: Exosomes are extracellular nano-vesicles measuring 30-200 nm, secreted by cells (especially MSCs and platelets). They contain mRNA, miRNA, and growth factors, making them useful for drug delivery, wound healing, and skin rejuvenation in dermatology.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male with Norwood Grade III androgenetic alopecia seeks hair transplantation. His donor density is 85 FU/cm² and he has no other medical conditions. What is the most appropriate advice regarding timing of surgery?
opts: Proceed with surgery as donor density is adequate
Defer surgery until age >25 years due to unpredictable future hair loss pattern
Perform surgery only if he starts finasteride immediately
Surgery is contraindicated as Norwood III is too advanced for transplantation
questions.exp: Hair transplant surgery is highly preferred for patients >25 years of age. In younger patients, the ultimate pattern and extent of hair loss are unpredictable, risking an unnatural appearance as balding progresses beyond the transplanted area.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes a nail matrix biopsy for longitudinal melanonychia. Post-operatively, she develops a permanent longitudinal split in her nail plate. Which anatomical structure was most likely injured during the procedure?
questions.exp: The nail matrix (germinal matrix) is the germinative center that produces the nail plate substance. Injury to the matrix causes permanent nail dystrophy including scarring, ridging, or splitting of the nail plate.

questions.q: Which pioneer is credited with developing the first working ruby laser?
questions.exp: Theodore Maiman developed the first working ruby laser in 1960. Gordon Gould was one of the inventors of the laser concept, C Kumar N Patel invented the CO2 laser, and Shimon Eckhouse developed IPL technology.

questions.q: During elliptical excision of a lesion, the surgeon notices tissue redundancy at the wound apices forming 'dog-ears'. Which geometric principle was most likely violated during the initial excision design?
opts: Length to width ratio less than 2:1
Long axis perpendicular to relaxed skin tension lines
Undermining performed in the wrong tissue plane
questions.exp: Dog-ears form when the apex angle exceeds 30 degrees. The optimal ellipse design requires apex angles ≤30° and a length-to-width ratio of at least 3:1 to prevent tissue redundancy at the wound ends.

questions.q: The principle of donor dominance in hair transplantation is based on which characteristic of occipital scalp hair follicles?
opts: Higher blood supply to dermal papilla cells
Absence of androgen receptors in dermal papilla cells
Increased melanocyte density in the hair bulb
questions.exp: Donor dominance, introduced by Orentreich in 1959, states that hair follicles in the occipital and temporal scalp genetically lack androgen receptors in their dermal papilla cells, making them resistant to DHT-induced miniaturization even after transplantation.

questions.q: A patient develops urticaria and bronchospasm shortly after receiving a local anesthetic injection. Skin prick testing reveals sensitivity to para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA). Which local anesthetic is the patient most likely to have received?
questions.exp: Procaine is an ester-type local anesthetic that is hydrolyzed by pseudocholinesterase to produce PABA, a known allergen responsible for Type I hypersensitivity reactions. Amide anesthetics like lidocaine, bupivacaine, and prilocaine do not produce PABA and rarely cause true allergic reactions.

questions.q: A 72-year-old woman presents with multiple thin actinic keratoses scattered across her forehead and scalp, consistent with field cancerization. She is concerned about cosmetic outcomes. Which treatment modality offers the best combination of field treatment capability and cosmetic outcome for this presentation?
questions.exp: PDT is the premier choice for field cancerization as it selectively destroys both subclinical and clinically visible lesions across large areas. It provides superior cosmetic outcomes compared to cryotherapy and 5-fluorouracil, with 75-90% complete clearance rates for thin to moderate AKs.
